classification.difficultyReason: Combine repairs, compound loan interest and profit, then reverse the combined multiplier.

content.prompt:
Andrea buys a house and she spends an extra $10\%$ of what she paid for the house on repairs. She takes out a loan and pays $5\%$ p.a. compound interest on the total amount spent (including repairs). Three years later she sells the house for $\$565\,100$ and she gains $20\%$ on the whole investment purchase price. How much did she pay for the house?

Include the accrued loan interest in the whole investment cost. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
$\$369\,814.11$.

Reverse the profit, compound-interest and repairs multipliers.
answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the original house price in dollars. The whole investment cost includes repairs and three years of accrued loan interest.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost including repairs}&=1.10P\\\text{Cost including interest}&=1.10P(1.05)^3\\\text{Sale price}&=1.20\times1.10P(1.05)^3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}565\,100&=1.20\times1.10P(1.05)^3\\P&=\frac{565\,100}{1.20\times1.10\times(1.05)^3}\\P&\approx369\,814.11\end{align*}$$

Andrea paid $\$369\,814.11$ for the house.
